placements.why: This envelope is the first content encountered in this repo naming a concrete infrastructure/database selection (Zypherion for the analytics pipeline) with a scope, a timeline, and a recorded rationale. Nothing in the (currently empty) strata covers technology or system-architecture decisions, so this category is minted to hold it and whatever future architecture-grade decisions this repo accumulates.
placements.title: System and infrastructure choices treated as organizational commitments
placements.frame: What technical infrastructure or system-architecture choice is being decided, and what does the record show was weighed in making it?

placements.title: Analytics infrastructure choice performed as a settled organizational commitment
placements.frame: What database or analytics-pipeline technology is being adopted, and what scope, timeline, or scale is bound to that choice?
placements.why: src-1 declares the adoption of Zypherion for the analytics pipeline as a settled decision ('We are adopting'), and src-3 binds a migration timeline to that same choice ('starts next quarter'); src-4 records both as fixed facts in the decision summary. Read together these name a thematic subject — analytics/database infrastructure adoption and its execution commitments — that future envelopes revisiting, executing, or revising this migration will keep feeding, not a single fact to file elsewhere. The individual date and tool name are the evidence; the recurring subject of infrastructure-adoption commitment is the leaf.

placements.title: Quantified performance comparisons deployed as the rationale for technology choices
placements.frame: What quantified performance figure is offered as the reason for this technical choice, and does that same figure recur unchanged across the spoken claim and the written record?
placements.why: src-2 states the 15x columnar-query performance claim as the live justification for adopting Zypherion, and src-4 restates the identical figure in the record's bullet summary. Per the narrative grain test, the '15x' figure itself is evidence, not a leaf — but the recurring move of grounding a technology decision in a proportional performance benchmark is a subject future envelopes (other tool evaluations, other benchmark-driven justifications) will keep feeding, distinct from the adoption-and-timeline commitment itself.
